blocks.title: Honors — three views, one motion
blocks.markdown: You've now built three ways to describe the same moving thing: a **graph** (position or velocity vs. time), an **equation** (the kinematics relations), and a **vector** (magnitude plus direction). The honors move today is to prove to yourself they're not three topics — they're one idea in three costumes.

## Connect backward — tie the three together

Look back across the last week and make the seams explicit:

- The **slope** of a position–time graph *is* the velocity in your equations *is* the magnitude-and-sign of your velocity vector. Same number, three faces.
- The **slope** of a velocity–time graph *is* the $a$ in $v = v_0 + at$ *is* how the velocity vector is changing.
- The **area** under a velocity–time graph *is* the $\Delta x$ that $\Delta x = v_0 t + \tfrac12 a t^2$ computes.

If you can read a value off the graph, you can find it from the equation, and you can point it as a vector. A motion you can only handle one way you don't really own yet — you've memorized a procedure, not understood the motion.

blocks.frame: On a velocity–time graph, the slope tells me ___ and the area tells me ___. The same two facts show up in my equations as ___ and ___, and as a vector they look like ___.
blocks.prompt: JUSTIFY (homework): Take one velocity–time graph from today. Read its slope and its area. Then show that the *same* two quantities fall out of the kinematics equations, and describe what each one is as a vector. Make the case that the graph, the equation, and the vector are telling one story — not three.

blocks.title: Close forward
blocks.markdown: You can now fully describe *how* something moves. What you still can't say is *why* it moves that way — what makes the velocity change at all. That 'why' has a name, and it's the next thing we build: **force.** Hold onto the question.
